newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RMB unit launches four international funds.
newsitem.headline: RMB unit launches four international funds.

text.p: South Africa's Rand Merchant Bank Unit Trusts said on Thursday it had launched four international funds aimed at exploiting the easing of foreign exchange controls on individuals on July 1.
The four funds, which would be listed on the Dublin Stock Exchange, are aimed at global equities, bonds and currencies as well as emerging markets.
The company said it had also launched an offshore deposit account based in Jersey, which would offer South Africans specially negotiated, high interest rates normally available only to corporates.

It noted that its Global Equity Fund had already been operating under the stewardship of Morgan Grenfell Asset Management since early 1996 and achieved a 42.9 percent investment return in rand terms in that year.
"We're confident that our offshore funds will set a new standard in the range of investment opportunities on offer to South African investors," marketing manager Stella Pengilly said.

South Africa's Finance Ministry has yet to announce the amount individuals will be allowed to invest offshore from July 1, although Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals said on Wednesday the limit was expected to be set at around 160,000 rand.
